verdict.rationale: Jitsu documents an HTTP API for sending data from your backend, authenticated with an `X-Write-Key` header. For delivery guarantees, it documents Kafka buffering while the warehouse is offline, deduplication of resent data, and a dead-letter queue whose failed events can be replayed. Missing for 10: endpoint-level detail of the ingestion API (payload schema, response and acknowledgement semantics), an explicit delivery-semantics statement tied to the ingestion endpoint (e.g. at-least-once), and independent or hands-on corroboration of server-to-server ingestion reliability.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I can send events server-to-server through a documented HTTP ingestion API with authentication and delivery guarantees

citations.quote: You can use HTTP API to send data to Jitsu. This is useful if you want to send data from your backend.
Jitsu will keep your data in a Kafka and deliver it once the warehouse is back online
Send same data as many times as you want. Jitsu will deduplicate it for you
Dead-letter queue with a reprocessing worker: failed events can be replayed instead of lost.
